key_insight: PointTPA generates input-aware (test-time) network parameters for each scene, allowing a single model to adapt dynamically to diverse 3D geometries and layouts during inference.
problem_solved: Static network parameters limit scene-level point cloud understanding—this work addresses adaptability to diverse geometries, imbalanced categories, and highly varied spatial layouts by adapting model parameters at test time.
method: Test-time Parameter Adaptation: a lightweight module generates input-conditioned network parameters for each scene during inference.
Serialization-based neighborhood encoding captures local and contextual geometry to inform the parameter generator.
Plug-and-play design that augments existing point-cloud backbones to improve robustness without full model retraining.
impact: Enables more robust, context-aware 3D scene understanding in real-world, heterogeneous point clouds—improving accuracy and generalization under distribution shifts while simplifying deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing a point-cloud input → serialization-based neighborhood encoder → parameter generator → adapted network → semantic output
Illustration of serialization/neighborhood encoding (ordered neighbor sequence or local patches) to convey how local context is captured
Before/after scene visualization (semantic segmentation maps) comparing static vs. PointTPA-adapted outputs
Bar/line chart showing robustness gains (e.g., accuracy or IoU) across classes, imbalance levels, or domain shifts
paper_title: PointTPA: Dynamic Network Parameter Adaptation for 3D Scene Understanding
paper_authors: Siyuan Liu, Chaoqun Zheng, Xin Zhou, Tianrui Feng, Dingkang Liang
